literal: Li Zhilian; Feng Shu; Xu Dun; Yang Lie; Yuan Biao
idiomatic: Li Zhilian; Feng Shu; Xu Dun; Yang Lie; Yuan Biao

literal: Li Zhilian, a man of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: Li Zhilian came from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

literal: Younger brother of Yishen, inspector of Qi province.
idiomatic: He was the younger brother of Yishen, inspector of Qi province.

literal: Zhilian from youth was few in desires; as a child he would not at first ask anything of his family.
idiomatic: Zhilian from youth was sparing in desire; as a child he would not ask his family for anything.

literal: His family once deliberately gave him gold and jewels; he never took them, and when they forced payment he would throw them to the ground.
idiomatic: His family once deliberately gave him gold and jewels; he never took them, and when they forced them on him he threw them to the ground.

literal: The provincial governor, because he was young and yet frugal, therefore named him Zhilian.
idiomatic: The provincial governor, because he was young and yet frugal, gave him the name Zhilian.

literal: Clever and fond of learning; at fifteen he had already gone through the chapter-and-commentary texts of the Five Classics.
idiomatic: Clever and fond of learning, at fifteen he had already worked through the chapter-and-commentary texts of the Five Classics.

literal: When Ge Rong rose in rebellion the native commandery was in turmoil; he fled the disaster and went to the capital.
idiomatic: When Ge Rong rose in rebellion the native commandery was in turmoil; he fled the troubles and went to the capital.

literal: In the Yong'an era he doffed commoner's dress and was made court gentleman attendant.
idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he left private life and was made court gentleman attendant.

literal: Early in Putai he was made establishment-office recorder, dragon-prancing general, and recorder in the Guangzhou expeditionary-south establishment office; he did not take office.
idiomatic: Early in Putai he was made establishment-office recorder, dragon-prancing general, and recorder in the Guangzhou expeditionary-south establishment office, but did not take office.

literal: Soon he was transferred to consulting aide in the establishment office and former general.
idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to consulting aide in the establishment office and former general.

literal: In the Tianping era Gao Huan promoted him to chief of staff in the Taizhou establishment office and general who pacifies the north.
idiomatic: In the Tianping era Gao Huan promoted him to chief of staff in the Taizhou establishment office and general who pacifies the north.

literal: Zhilian harmonized officers and men; army and people were pleased.
idiomatic: Zhilian harmonized officers and men, and army and people were pleased.

literal: Gao Huan frequently visited Hedong and greatly admired him in sighs of praise.
idiomatic: Gao Huan frequently visited Hedong and greatly admired him, praising him aloud.

literal: He was transferred to chief of staff in Gao Cheng's swift-cavalry establishment office.
idiomatic: He was transferred to chief of staff in Gao Cheng's swift-cavalry establishment office.

literal: An edict said that because Jizhou controlled rivers and roads and received Liang envoys, an especially capable man was needed; Gao Cheng recommended him, and he was made acting chief of staff in Jizhou with insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: An edict said that because Jizhou controlled rivers and roads and received Liang envoys, an especially capable man was needed. Gao Cheng recommended him, and he was made acting chief of staff in Jizhou with insignia equal to the three excellencies.

literal: He was again moved to chief of staff in Ying province.
idiomatic: He was again moved to chief of staff in Ying province.

literal: Gao Huan was passing through Ji province and gathered the documents of the six Hebei provinces to compare and verify increases and decreases in household registers.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was passing through Ji province and gathered the documents of the six Hebei provinces to compare and verify increases and decreases in household registers.

literal: Gao Huan personally directed the work, mostly on horseback, demanding documents and pointing to scenes to require completeness—affairs of many kinds.
idiomatic: Gao Huan personally directed the work, mostly on horseback, demanding documents and pointing to scenes to require completeness—affairs of many kinds.

literal: Zhilian each time responded on the spot and finished at once, always meeting the deadline in advance; nothing failed to match the deep intent, and he became the standard for all provinces.
idiomatic: Zhilian each time responded on the spot and finished at once, always meeting the deadline in advance; nothing failed to match the deep intent, and he became the standard for all provinces.

literal: Gao Huan turned to Sima Ziru and said: "Watch how Zhilian disposes affairs—it satisfies the mind.
idiomatic: Gao Huan turned to Sima Ziru and said, "Watch how Zhilian disposes affairs—it satisfies the mind.

literal: " He then gathered civil and military officials numbering tens of thousands, had gentleman Du Bi proclaim the edict to comfort and reward them, and still questioned the chiefs of staff, magistrates, and the rest of the provinces; all others bowed in confession of fault, but Zhilian alone stepped forward to bow in thanks for grace, and the onlookers all sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: " He then gathered civil and military officials numbering tens of thousands, had gentleman Du Bi proclaim the edict to comfort and reward them, and still questioned the chiefs of staff, magistrates, and the rest of the provinces. All others bowed in confession of fault, but Zhilian alone stepped forward to bow in thanks for grace, and the onlookers all sighed in admiration.

literal: That day he was granted oxen and wine.
idiomatic: That day he was granted oxen and wine.

literal: Gao Huan returned to Bing and told Gao Cheng of the affair.
idiomatic: Gao Huan returned to Bing and told Gao Cheng of the affair.

literal: Gao Cheng was pleased and told others: "I am quite able to know men."
idiomatic: Gao Cheng was pleased and told others, "I am quite able to know men."

literal: When Gao Cheng took up affairs he summoned Zhilian to Jinyang and made him a staff member of the hegemon's office.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took up affairs he summoned Zhilian to Jinyang and made him a staff member of the hegemon's office.

literal: He told Du Bi: "Bingzhou is the king's foundation; a good chief of staff is needed—each of you recommend someone you know.
idiomatic: He told Du Bi, "Bingzhou is the king's foundation; a good chief of staff is needed—each of you recommend someone you know.

literal: " At the time each recommended someone else; none was approved.
idiomatic: " At the time each recommended someone else; none was approved.

literal: The crowd had not yet answered.
idiomatic: The crowd had not yet answered.

literal: Gao Cheng then told Chen Yuankang: "I will teach you where to find a good chief of staff—Li Zhilian is the man.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng then told Chen Yuankang, "I will teach you where to find a good chief of staff—Li Zhilian is the man.

literal: " He then appointed him chief of staff in Bing province.
idiomatic: " He then appointed him chief of staff in Bing province.

literal: He was constantly within Gao Cheng's residence, and with Xin Shu of Longxi and five others was called lodge guests, treated with the courtesy due a superior guest.
idiomatic: He was constantly within Gao Cheng's residence, and with Xin Shu of Longxi and five others was called lodge guests, treated with the courtesy due a superior guest.

literal: Feng Shu, styled Junyi, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.
idiomatic: Feng Shu, styled Junyi, came from Tiao in Bohai.

literal: His father Gui was director of the court of justice and inspector of Ji province.
idiomatic: His father Gui was director of the court of justice and inspector of Ji province.

literal: Shu had administrative ability; at eighteen he was armor-bureau aide in the Ji province expeditionary-east establishment office.
idiomatic: Shu had administrative ability; at eighteen he was armor-bureau aide in the Ji province expeditionary-east establishment office.

literal: Gao Daomu was attendant censor-in-chief and opened a post for him as censor.
idiomatic: Gao Daomu was attendant censor-in-chief and opened a post for him as censor.

literal: He was moved to recorder in Prince of Qinghe's grand-marshal establishment office, concurrently chief clerk in the ministry of the masses.
idiomatic: He was moved to recorder in Prince of Qinghe's grand-marshal establishment office, concurrently chief clerk in the ministry of the masses.

literal: In the Taichang era he was made gentleman in the ministry of the three excellencies; he was known as fair and capable.
idiomatic: In the Taichang era he was made gentleman in the ministry of the three excellencies; he was known as fair and capable.

literal: In the Tianping era he revised old precedents into the New Statutes of the Linzhi Hall; its legal articles and clauses were all edited and fixed by Shu.
idiomatic: In the Tianping era he revised old precedents into the New Statutes of the Linzhi Hall; its legal articles and clauses were all edited and fixed by Shu.

literal: Liang scattered-cavalry regular attendant Lu Yanzi and Shen Jing came on embassy; Shu was made concurrent direct-communication gentleman and sent to Liang.
idiomatic: Liang scattered-cavalry regular attendant Lu Yanzi and Shen Jing came on embassy; Shu was made concurrent direct-communication gentleman and sent to Liang.

literal: On return he was moved to aide in Gao Cheng's great-general establishment office and overseer of capital-district affairs.
idiomatic: On return he was moved to aide in Gao Cheng's great-general establishment office and overseer of capital-district affairs.

literal: In the fifth Wuding year he was made administrator of Pengcheng and supervisor of that commandery, and again acting inspector of eastern Xuzhou.
idiomatic: In the fifth Wuding year he was made administrator of Pengcheng and supervisor of that commandery, and again acting inspector of eastern Xuzhou.

literal: In the seventh Wuding year he was made vice director of the court of justice.
idiomatic: In the seventh Wuding year he was made vice director of the court of justice.

literal: In the eighth year he was concurrently supervising gentleman of the yellow gate.
idiomatic: In the eighth year he was concurrently supervising gentleman of the yellow gate.

literal: When Qi received the mandate he, with Li Jiang and seven others, served as great envoys touring the regions to inquire into local customs and ask after the people's hardships.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate he, with Li Jiang and seven others, served as great envoys touring the regions to inquire into local customs and ask after the people's hardships.

literal: In the third Tianbao year he was made administrator of Qinghe, moved to left chief of staff in the ministry of the masses, acting director of eastern-capital affairs, and soon made inspector of Haizhou.
idiomatic: In the third Tianbao year he was made administrator of Qinghe, moved to left chief of staff in the ministry of the masses, acting director of eastern-capital affairs, and soon made inspector of Haizhou.

literal: In the first Daning year he was summoned and appointed director of the great court of justice.
idiomatic: In the first Daning year he was summoned and appointed director of the great court of justice.

literal: In the third Heqing year an edict ordered him together with recorder of the masters of writing Zhao Yanshen, vice director Wei Shou, minister Yang Xiuzhi, and director of the imperial academy Ma Jingde and others to deliberate on laws and ordinances.
idiomatic: In the third Heqing year an edict ordered him together with recorder of the masters of writing Zhao Yanshen, vice director Wei Shou, minister Yang Xiuzhi, and director of the imperial academy Ma Jingde and others to deliberate on laws and ordinances.

literal: In the first Tiantong year he was moved to director of the revenue ministry.
idiomatic: In the first Tiantong year he was moved to director of the revenue ministry.

literal: In the third year he was transferred to director of the five armies ministry and given added rank as acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to director of the five armies ministry and given added rank as acting insignia equal to the three excellencies.

literal: In the first Wuping year he was made inspector of southern Yanzhou.
idiomatic: In the first Wuping year he was made inspector of southern Yanzhou.

literal: When his term ended he returned to court and was made left grand master of gleaming fortune, then again director in the palace ministry.
idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to court and was made left grand master of gleaming fortune, then again director in the palace ministry.

literal: Shu long served as a judicial officer, clearly understanding statutes and ordinances; his deliberations and judgments were fair and even, and he was deeply praised by men of the time.
idiomatic: Shu long served as a judicial officer, clearly understanding statutes and ordinances; his deliberations and judgments were fair and even, and he was deeply praised by men of the time.

literal: Yet he amassed wealth in great store and made not a single gift; even to the closest friends, when poor, ill, and in desperate straits, he cut off all relief—court and countryside alike in public talk greatly despised him.
idiomatic: Yet he amassed wealth in great store and made not a single gift; even to the closest friends, when poor, ill, and in desperate straits, he cut off all relief—court and countryside alike in public talk greatly despised him.

literal: Outwardly his appearance was square and orderly, yet he could not avoid private petitions; in avoiding and advancing he often drew sneers of shock.
idiomatic: Outwardly his appearance was square and orderly, yet he could not avoid private petitions; in avoiding and advancing he often drew sneers of shock.

literal: His former wife was of the Sima clan of Henei; he had one son, for whom he took in marriage the daughter of Li Shiyuan of Longxi and lavished bride-price wealth.
idiomatic: His former wife was of the Sima clan of Henei; he had one son, for whom he took in marriage the daughter of Li Shiyuan of Longxi and lavished bride-price wealth.

literal: When the rites were about to be completed they still disputed and hung in delay.
idiomatic: When the rites were about to be completed they still disputed and hung in delay.

literal: Shu suddenly took an offering image and faced Shiyuan, striking the image to swear; Shiyuan laughed and said: "Lord Feng, where do you always get emergency images, that you need a vow and use one at once?
idiomatic: Shu suddenly took an offering image and faced Shiyuan, striking the image to swear; Shiyuan laughed and said, "Lord Feng, where do you always get emergency images, that you need a vow and use one at once?

literal: " His son took in marriage the daughter of Lu Zhuangzhi of Fanyang.
idiomatic: " His son took in marriage the daughter of Lu Zhuangzhi of Fanyang.

literal: Shu again went straight to the government office to complain, saying: "The mules sent were faulted as lame in the leg; when fields were appraised they were said to be salty and thin; bronze vessels too were faulted as old and worn out."
idiomatic: Shu again went straight to the government office to complain, saying, "The mules sent were faulted as lame in the leg; when fields were appraised they were said to be salty and thin; bronze vessels too were faulted as old and worn out."

literal: All were matters touched by his stinginess, and each time brought turmoil.
idiomatic: All were matters touched by his stinginess, and each time brought turmoil.

literal: His son Yuan, at the end of Wuping, was crown-prince attendant.
idiomatic: His son Yuan, at the end of Wuping, was crown-prince attendant.

literal: Shu's younger brother Xun, styled Jingwen.
idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Xun, styled Jingwen.

literal: Wei outer-office gentleman; in Wuding he was law-bureau aide in Prince of Yong'an's establishment office, gradually moved to gentleman in the ministry of works' establishment section, transferred to gentleman of the three excellencies, went out as administrator of eastern Pingyuan commandery, moved to chief of staff in Ding province, again made administrator of Hejian commandery, entered court as left director in the masters of writing, and again administrator of Jinan.
idiomatic: Wei outer-office gentleman; in Wuding he was law-bureau aide in Prince of Yong'an's establishment office, gradually moved to gentleman in the ministry of works' establishment section, transferred to gentleman of the three excellencies, went out as administrator of eastern Pingyuan commandery, moved to chief of staff in Ding province, again made administrator of Hejian commandery, entered court as left director in the masters of writing, and again administrator of Jinan.

literal: He died in the Kaihuang era of Sui.
idiomatic: He died in the Kaihuang era of Sui.

literal: Xun ranged through the classics and histories, held himself in pure simplicity, and in every office had administrative talent and equipment; in governing commanderies his reputation and achievement were very marked, and officials and people respected and loved him.
idiomatic: Xun ranged through the classics and histories, held himself in pure simplicity, and in every office had administrative talent and equipment; in governing commanderies his reputation and achievement were very marked, and officials and people respected and loved him.

literal: Xu Dun, styled Jiliang, was a man of Xincheng in Gaoyang.
idiomatic: Xu Dun, styled Jiliang, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang.

literal: His father Hu was Wei administrator of Gaoyang and Zhangwu commanderies.
idiomatic: His father Hu was Wei administrator of Gaoyang and Zhangwu commanderies.

literal: Dun had clear judgment and quick wit, skilled in government; he served as chief clerk in the ministry of the masses and was known for his ability to decide cases; men of the time called him the Iron-Entering Registrar.
idiomatic: Dun had clear judgment and quick wit, skilled in government; he served as chief clerk in the ministry of the masses and was known for his ability to decide cases; men of the time called him the Iron-Entering Registrar.

literal: He was gradually moved to administrator of Yangping.
idiomatic: He was gradually moved to administrator of Yangping.

literal: At the time the capital was moved to Ye; Yangping was then a metropolitan commandery, and military and state requisitions and tax levies had no standard; moreover meritorious nobles made requests, seeking day and night—Dun governed all by principle, above and below without resentment, and his governance ranked first under Heaven.
idiomatic: At the time the capital was moved to Ye; Yangping was then a metropolitan commandery, and military and state requisitions and tax levies had no standard; moreover meritorious nobles made requests, seeking day and night—Dun governed all by principle, above and below without resentment, and his governance ranked first under Heaven.

literal: He received special reward and distinction; his likeness was painted at the palace gate and an edict distributed it throughout the realm.
idiomatic: He received special reward and distinction; his likeness was painted at the palace gate and an edict distributed it throughout the realm.

literal: He was moved to metropolitan magistrate of Wei, went out and received appointment as inspector of Qi province, transferred to inspector of Liang province—wherever he governed there was reputation.
idiomatic: He was moved to metropolitan magistrate of Wei, went out and received appointment as inspector of Qi province, transferred to inspector of Liang province—wherever he governed there was reputation.

literal: He was moved to grand director of agriculture.
idiomatic: He was moved to grand director of agriculture.

literal: It happened that Hou Jing rebelled; Wang Sizheng entered and held Ying city; the royal army went out to attack; Dun constantly supervised transport, and the army never lacked supplies.
idiomatic: It happened that Hou Jing rebelled; Wang Sizheng entered and held Ying city; the royal army went out to attack; Dun constantly supervised transport, and the army never lacked supplies.

literal: Drawing the Wei River to flood the city was also Dun's stratagem.
idiomatic: Drawing the Wei River to flood the city was also Dun's stratagem.

literal: He was moved to director in the palace ministry.
idiomatic: He was moved to director in the palace ministry.

literal: Dun had a fine beard hanging down to his belt; within the ministry he was called the Long-Beard Lord.
idiomatic: Dun had a fine beard hanging down to his belt; within the ministry he was called the Long-Beard Lord.

literal: Gao Yang once, when drunk with wine, grasped Dun's beard and praised it, then took a knife and cut it off, leaving only one handful.
idiomatic: Gao Yang once, when drunk with wine, grasped Dun's beard and praised it, then took a knife and cut it off, leaving only one handful.

literal: Dun was afraid and therefore no longer dared let it grow long; men of the time again called him the Trimmed-Beard Lord.
idiomatic: Dun was afraid and therefore no longer dared let it grow long; men of the time again called him the Trimmed-Beard Lord.

literal: When Gao Yan ascended the throne he led the attendant censorate and was inspector of Jiao province.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan ascended the throne he led the attendant censorate and was inspector of Jiao province.

literal: Soon he was recalled as director of the ministry of agriculture, again moved to director of the great court of justice, again director of the revenue ministry, and served in succession as junior guardian and junior tutor of the heir apparent, grand master of gleaming fortune, acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, right vice director of the masters of writing, and specially advanced; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wannian county with dry fief salary from Xiapi commandery.
idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as director of the ministry of agriculture, again moved to director of the great court of justice, again director of the revenue ministry, and served in succession as junior guardian and junior tutor of the heir apparent, grand master of gleaming fortune, acting insignia equal to the three excellencies, right vice director of the masters of writing, and specially advanced; he was enfeoffed as baron of Wannian county with dry fief salary from Xiapi commandery.

literal: Because of old age he retired to his home and died three years later.
idiomatic: Because of old age he retired to his home and died three years later.

literal: Dun in youth was pure and upright; in later years he became more restless.
idiomatic: Dun in youth was pure and upright; in later years he became more restless.

literal: In Qi court practice the great impartial selector of the native commandery was held by a capital official.
idiomatic: In Qi court practice the great impartial selector of the native commandery was held by a capital official.

literal: Xing Shao of the same commandery was supervisor of the secretariat; his virtue and standing were very high; Dun competed with Shao for the impartial selector post and therefore clung to Song Qindao, having Shao sent out as inspector; court opinion greatly despised him for it.
idiomatic: Xing Shao of the same commandery was supervisor of the secretariat; his virtue and standing were very high; Dun competed with Shao for the impartial selector post and therefore clung to Song Qindao, having Shao sent out as inspector; court opinion greatly despised him for it.

literal: Though he long walked the court ranks and held clear, eminent offices, standing shoulder to shoulder with Xing Shao, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Jie, Xu Zhicai, and the like—some discussed the classics and histories, some chanted poetry and rhapsodies, mocking one another in turn with laughter filling the hall—Dun did not understand lively talk and had no learning; sometimes he sat the whole time with sealed lips, sometimes hid behind a desk and slept, and was deeply slighted by the leading circles.
idiomatic: Though he long walked the court ranks and held clear, eminent offices, standing shoulder to shoulder with Xing Shao, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Jie, Xu Zhicai, and the like—some discussed the classics and histories, some chanted poetry and rhapsodies, mocking one another in turn with laughter filling the hall—Dun did not understand lively talk and had no learning; sometimes he sat the whole time with sealed lips, sometimes hid behind a desk and slept, and was deeply slighted by the leading circles.

literal: His son Wenji, at the end of Wuping, was gentleman in the revenue ministry.
idiomatic: His son Wenji, at the end of Wuping, was gentleman in the revenue ministry.

literal: Wenji's younger brother Wenjing was diligent in study, square and refined in manner, with no choice in personal conduct and no jesting words on his lips.
idiomatic: Wenji's younger brother Wenjing was diligent in study, square and refined in manner, with no choice in personal conduct and no jesting words on his lips.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was attendant censor within the palace.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was attendant censor within the palace.

literal: Early in Sui Kaihuang he was attendant censor, concurrently regular attendant for direct communication, deputy on embassy to Chen, and director of the ministry of enfeoffments.
idiomatic: Early in Sui Kaihuang he was attendant censor, concurrently regular attendant for direct communication, deputy on embassy to Chen, and director of the ministry of enfeoffments.

literal: He died as chief of staff in Xiang province.
idiomatic: He died as chief of staff in Xiang province.

literal: Dun's elder brother Xun, styled Zhongrang, had administrative talent; in the Qianming era he was administrator of Pingyuan and on death was posthumously given inspector of Xin province.
idiomatic: Dun's elder brother Xun, styled Zhongrang, had administrative talent; in the Qianming era he was administrator of Pingyuan and on death was posthumously given inspector of Xin province.

literal: Xun's son Wengao was a staff member in the ministry of the masses.
idiomatic: Xun's son Wengao was a staff member in the ministry of the masses.

literal: Yang Lie, styled Xinqing, was a man of Juping in Mount Tai.
idiomatic: Yang Lie, styled Xinqing, came from Juping in Mount Tai.

literal: Eighth-generation descendant of Xiu, grand master of the imperial stud in Jin; nephew of Zhi, Liang inspector.
idiomatic: Eighth-generation descendant of Xiu, grand master of the imperial stud in Jin; nephew of Zhi, Liang inspector.

literal: His father Lingzhen was Wei vice-director in Yan province.
idiomatic: His father Lingzhen was Wei vice-director in Yan province.

literal: Lie from youth was penetrating and quick, self-cultivating in conduct, with the bearing of a mature man.
idiomatic: Lie from youth was penetrating and quick, self-cultivating in conduct, with the bearing of a mature man.

literal: Fond of reading books, able to discourse on essential principles, he was known for Dark Learning.
idiomatic: Fond of reading books, able to discourse on essential principles, he was known for Dark Learning.

literal: In the Wei Xiaochang era Lie's elder cousin by the mother's side Kan was administrator and, holding the commandery, raised troops in external rebellion.
idiomatic: In the Wei Xiaochang era Lie's elder cousin by the mother's side Kan was administrator and, holding the commandery, raised troops in external rebellion.
